statements.status_notes: IO::Uncompress::Unzip versions before 2.215 for Perl propagate an uncaught exception when parsing a zip header with a malformed DOS date. The _dosToUnixTime() function calls Time::Local::timelocal() without an eval guard; a header whose date field decodes to an out-of-range month, day, or hour causes the exception to propagate out of the caller, which expects undef plus an error variable instead.
statements.impact_statement: Perl's IO::Uncompress::Unzip propagates an uncaught exception when a zip header's DOS date field decodes to an out-of-range value. The container's entrypoint execs only the Liquibase CLI directly (a Java process, not a shell script that shells out to Perl), and a source review found no invocation of perl or any Perl module anywhere in Liquibase's build or runtime. This OS package's version is not pinned by this repository — it tracks whatever the unversioned eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble base image tag resolves to at build time. Confirmed by pulling the current base image directly and checking installed package versions (not from repo-pinned config), it ships perl-base 5.38.2-3.2ubuntu0.4, the fixed release, as additional defense-in-depth.

statements.status_notes: Socket versions before 2.041 for Perl have an out-of-bounds heap read. pack_ip_mreq_source() in Socket.xs validates argument lengths in the wrong order, so a source address shorter than 4 bytes is not rejected and the copy reads up to 3 bytes past the end of its buffer, leaking adjacent heap memory into the packed structure.
statements.impact_statement: An out-of-bounds heap read exists in Perl's Socket module (pack_ip_mreq_source() in Socket.xs) when an application calls it with a multicast source address shorter than 4 bytes. Liquibase never invokes Perl or any Perl module (see the CVE-2025-15649 assessment on this same subcomponent for the reachability evidence). This OS package's version is not pinned by this repository — it tracks whatever the unversioned eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble base image tag resolves to at build time. Confirmed by pulling the current base image directly and checking installed package versions (not from repo-pinned config), it ships perl-base 5.38.2-3.2ubuntu0.4, the fixed release, as additional defense-in-depth.

statements.status_notes: Perl through version 5.43.9 has a regex overflow flaw. When an alternation compiled into a trie by Perl_study_chunk contains more than 65,535 branches, a 16-bit delta field overflows and the trie's match decision table is silently truncated with no warning, causing the regex to return both false positives and false negatives.
statements.impact_statement: Perl's regex compiler silently truncates its match table when an alternation has more than 65,535 branches, producing incorrect (false-positive and false-negative) pattern matches — a risk only when such a regex gates an access-control or input-filtering decision. Liquibase never invokes Perl or any Perl module (see the CVE-2025-15649 assessment on this same subcomponent for the reachability evidence), so no Liquibase security control is implemented via a Perl regex. This OS package's version is not pinned by this repository — it tracks whatever the unversioned eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble base image tag resolves to at build time. Confirmed by pulling the current base image directly and checking installed package versions (not from repo-pinned config), it ships perl-base 5.38.2-3.2ubuntu0.4, the fixed release, as additional defense-in-depth.

statements.status_notes: Perl versions through 5.45.1 have out-of-bounds heap reads and writes during regular expression matching via an undersized superlinear cache in S_regmatch. A caller that matches an attacker-controlled subject of the required size and pattern shape can crash the process or corrupt heap memory.
statements.impact_statement: This regex-engine heap read/write flaw is reachable only when an application performs Perl regular-expression matching on attacker supplied subject strings. The container entrypoint execs only the Liquibase Java CLI directly (`docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:8`, `docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:119`), and a focused grep across the runtime Dockerfiles and entrypoint scripts found no perl invocation. The vulnerable Perl regex path is therefore not reachable from the stock Liquibase Secure runtime.

statements.status_notes: Perl versions from 5.9.4 before 5.41.9 can produce incorrect regular expression match results when a stale failure flag ends the Aho-Corasick prescan early in S_find_byclass, which can make access or filtering decisions wrong.
statements.impact_statement: This incorrect-match issue affects Perl's regex prescan logic and is relevant only when an application performs Perl regular-expression matching on attacker-controlled data and then makes a security decision from the result. The container entrypoint execs only the Liquibase Java CLI directly (`docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:8`, `docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:119`), and a focused grep across the runtime Dockerfiles and entrypoint scripts found no perl invocation. The vulnerable Perl regex path is not reachable in the stock runtime.

statements.status_notes: Archive::Tar versions before 3.08 for Perl extract symlinks with attacker controlled targets outside the extraction directory. _make_special_file() passes the tar header's linkname to symlink() without validating it against absolute paths or .. segments. The secure-extract mode check that guards regular file extraction does not cover the symlink target. A subsequent open through the extracted name reads or writes the attacker chosen path.
statements.impact_statement: The scanner reported perl-base 5.38.2-3.2ubuntu0.2 and the Ubuntu fix level is 5.38.2-3.2ubuntu0.3. This issue requires an application to invoke Perl Archive::Tar extraction on attacker-controlled archives so a crafted symlink target is created outside the extraction directory. Liquibase Secure's stock container starts the Java CLI directly, and a review of the runtime Dockerfiles and entrypoint scripts found no Perl invocation or Perl-based tar extraction path. The vulnerable Archive::Tar symlink-extraction path is therefore not reachable from the stock runtime.

statements.status_notes: Archive::Tar versions before 3.08 for Perl extract hardlinks to attacker controlled paths outside the extraction directory. _make_special_file() passes the tar header's linkname to link() without validating it against absolute paths or .. segments, creating a hardlink that shares the victim file's inode. A subsequent write through the extracted name modifies the victim file, and the post-extraction chmod, chown, and utime block in _extract_file() applies the tar header's mode, owner, and timestamps to the shared inode during extraction alone.
statements.impact_statement: The scanner reported perl-base 5.38.2-3.2ubuntu0.2 and the Ubuntu fix level is 5.38.2-3.2ubuntu0.3. This issue requires an application to invoke Perl Archive::Tar extraction on attacker-controlled archives so a crafted hardlink is created outside the extraction directory. Liquibase Secure's stock container starts the Java CLI directly, and a review of the runtime Dockerfiles and entrypoint scripts found no Perl invocation or Perl-based tar extraction path. The vulnerable Archive::Tar hardlink-extraction path is therefore not reachable from the stock runtime.

statements.status_notes: IO::Uncompress::Unzip versions before 2.220 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via per-byte read loop in fastForward. fastForward() compares length $offset (the digit count of the offset, 1 to 19) against the chunk size $c instead of $offset itself, so $c shrinks from 16 KiB to 1-19 bytes per iteration. Extracting a named entry from an attacker supplied zip via IO::Uncompress::Unzip->new($zip, Name => $target) drives a per-byte read loop scaling with the entry's compressed size, up to the non-Zip64 4 GiB cap.
statements.impact_statement: The scanner reported perl-base 5.38.2-3.2ubuntu0.2 and a fix level of 5.38.2-3.2ubuntu0.4. This issue requires an application to invoke Perl's IO::Uncompress::Unzip on attacker-supplied zip input so the vulnerable fastForward path is exercised. Liquibase Secure's stock container starts the Java CLI directly, and a review of the runtime Dockerfiles, entrypoint scripts, and application sources found no Perl invocation and no use of IO::Uncompress::Unzip. The vulnerable Perl zip extraction path is therefore not reachable from the stock runtime.

statements.status_notes: IO::Compress versions before 2.220 for Perl can execute arbitrary code in File::GlobMapper via an attacker-controlled output glob. _parseOutputGlob() wraps the caller-supplied output glob string in double quotes and stores it in the parser state; _getFiles() then runs the stored expression through eval STRING. A literal double quote in the output glob closes the dquote wrapper, and the characters that follow are evaluated as Perl. Arbitrary Perl in the output glob executes at the calling process's privilege.
statements.impact_statement: The scanner reported perl-base 5.38.2-3.2ubuntu0.2 and a fix level of 5.38.2-3.2ubuntu0.4. This issue requires an application to invoke Perl's IO::Compress output-glob handling so attacker-controlled glob text reaches File::GlobMapper and eval STRING. Liquibase Secure's stock container starts the Java CLI directly, and a review of the runtime Dockerfiles, entrypoint scripts, and application sources found no Perl invocation and no use of IO::Compress or File::GlobMapper. The vulnerable Perl compression path is therefore not reachable from the stock runtime.

statements.status_notes: Perl versions before 5.40.5-RC1, from 5.41.0 before 5.42.3-RC1, from 5.43.0 before 5.43.11 have an integer overflow in S_measure_struct leading to an out-of-bounds heap read in pack and unpack. S_measure_struct adds each item's size times its repeat count to a running total with no overflow check, so a large repeat count in a pack or unpack template wraps the signed SSize_t total negative. The @, X, and x position codes then guard their moves with a signed length comparison that passes when the length is negative, advancing the buffer pointer out of bounds. A template derived from untrusted input can read heap memory past the buffer and return it to the caller.
statements.impact_statement: perl-base is an Essential Ubuntu package, so /usr/bin/perl is present in every Liquibase Secure image, but nothing in the runtime path executes it: the container entrypoint and the liquibase launcher script contain no perl invocation, the Liquibase CLI is a Java process, and lpm is a statically linked Go binary. The vulnerable pack and unpack template parser only runs inside a Perl process handed an attacker-controlled template, so it is not reachable from Liquibase Secure. Fixed in Ubuntu perl-base 5.34.0-3ubuntu1.8 (jammy, shipped by Liquibase Secure 5.0.0 and 5.0.1) and 5.38.2-3.2ubuntu0.4 (noble, Liquibase Secure 5.0.2 through 5.2.1); Liquibase Secure 5.2.2 ships 5.38.2-3.2ubuntu0.6.

statements.status_notes: Storable versions before 3.41 for Perl have a signed integer overflow when deserializing a crafted SX_HOOK record. retrieve_hook_common reads a signed 32-bit item count from an SX_HOOK record and calls av_extend with that count plus one. A count of I32_MAX wraps the addition to a negative value. A crafted blob passed to thaw or retrieve triggers the overflow; av_extend receives the negative count and dies with a panic, terminating the deserialization.
statements.impact_statement: perl-base is an Essential Ubuntu package, so /usr/bin/perl is present in every Liquibase Secure image, but nothing in the runtime path executes it: the container entrypoint and the liquibase launcher script contain no perl invocation, the Liquibase CLI is a Java process, and lpm is a statically linked Go binary. The vulnerable Storable deserializer only runs inside a Perl process that thaws attacker-controlled data, so it is not reachable from Liquibase Secure. Fixed in Ubuntu perl-base 5.34.0-3ubuntu1.8 (jammy, shipped by Liquibase Secure 5.0.0 and 5.0.1) and 5.38.2-3.2ubuntu0.4 (noble, Liquibase Secure 5.0.2 through 5.2.1); Liquibase Secure 5.2.2 ships 5.38.2-3.2ubuntu0.6.

statements.impact_statement: NVD/Ubuntu list this id as REJECTED -- a duplicate of CVE-2026-14803, which describes an issue in libmojolicious-perl, not perl-base (likely a scanner package mismatch). Regardless, nothing in this repository or docker-entrypoint.sh shells out to perl.

statements.status_notes: HTTP::Tiny versions before 0.095 for Perl forward credential headers to cross-origin redirect targets. When the server returns a 3xx redirect, the caller's Authorization, Cookie and Proxy-Authorization headers are re-sent to whatever host the redirect names, across scheme, host or port boundaries, including https to http downgrades that expose them in plaintext on the wire.
statements.impact_statement: Scanner package misattribution. The vulnerable code is the HTTP::Tiny module, which Ubuntu ships in perl-modules (and libhttp-tiny-perl), not in perl-base. Neither package is installed in any Liquibase Secure image: perl-base carries only the interpreter and a minimal core module set, there is no HTTP/Tiny.pm anywhere on the image, and loading HTTP::Tiny fails with "Can't locate HTTP/Tiny.pm". The scanner matched a fix in the perl source package to perl-base, which does not contain the vulnerable module. Even setting that aside, nothing in the runtime path executes perl. Ubuntu fixes this in perl 5.38.2-3.2ubuntu0.4 (noble); jammy has no fix yet.

statements.impact_statement: NVD/Ubuntu list this id as REJECTED -- a duplicate of CVE-2026-15747, which describes an issue in libmojolicious-perl, not perl-base (likely a scanner package mismatch). Regardless, nothing in this repository or docker-entrypoint.sh shells out to perl.

statements.status_notes: Pod::Text versions before 6.1.1 for Perl allow CPU and memory exhaustion formatting a POD document whose =over nesting drives the margin to the output width. Each =over adds its indent to the margin, which wrap() subtracts from the output width to get the space available for text. When that space reaches zero, the line-splitting substitution matches the empty string, and the loop consumes no input while appending the margin padding on every pass. Formatting an attacker-supplied POD document never returns, and the output grows until memory is exhausted.
statements.impact_statement: Pod::Text (bundled with perl-base) CPU/memory exhaustion formatting a crafted POD document. Nothing in this repository or docker-entrypoint.sh shells out to perl or invokes POD formatting (pod2text/perldoc); the entrypoint does its own pattern matching with bash case/glob syntax.

statements.status_notes: Perl versions before 5.40.5-RC1, from 5.41.0 before 5.42.3-RC1, from 5.43.0 before 5.43.11 have a heap buffer overflow when compiling regular expressions with a repeated fixed string on 32-bit builds. A caller that compiles an attacker-controlled regular expression on a 32-bit perl build triggers a heap buffer overflow at compile time.
statements.impact_statement: The heap overflow only exists on 32-bit Perl builds compiling an attacker-controlled regular expression. Liquibase Secure images are published only for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, and the shipped perl is a 64-bit build (pointer size 8). In addition, nothing in the runtime path executes perl: the container entrypoint and the liquibase launcher script contain no perl invocation, the Liquibase CLI is a Java process, and lpm is a statically linked Go binary. Fixed in Ubuntu perl-base 5.34.0-3ubuntu1.7 (jammy, Liquibase Secure 5.0.0 and 5.0.1 shipped 5.34.0-3ubuntu1.5) and 5.38.2-3.2ubuntu0.3 (noble, Liquibase Secure 5.0.2 through 5.2.1 shipped 5.38.2-3.2ubuntu0.2); Liquibase Secure 5.2.2 and later ship 5.38.2-3.2ubuntu0.6.

statements.status_notes: Archive::Tar versions before 3.10 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via an attacker-controlled entry size field in a tar header. A crafted header declaring a multi-gigabyte size causes Perl to allocate a scalar of that size.
statements.impact_statement: Scanner package misattribution. The vulnerable code is the Archive::Tar module, which Ubuntu ships in perl-modules, not in perl-base. perl-modules is not installed in any Liquibase Secure image: perl-base carries only the interpreter and a minimal core module set, there is no Archive/Tar.pm anywhere on the image, and loading Archive::Tar fails with "Can't locate Archive/Tar.pm". The scanner matched a fix in the perl source package to perl-base, which does not contain the vulnerable module. Even setting that aside, nothing in the runtime path executes perl. Ubuntu fixes this in perl 5.38.2-3.2ubuntu0.4 (noble); jammy has no fix yet.
